0.5.0.0.added:
- Auto-Build Graph property (Auto / From Pathfinding / From Solids): zero-event startup — the obstacle map and graph build themselves on layout start.
- Tile Size auto-detect (0 = auto): reads the Pathfinding behavior's Cell Size or the solid tilemap's tile size, and propagates it to all shared-graph instances.
- New simple 'Find path' (X, Y) and 'Find path to object' actions with sensible defaults (ground correction on, Nearest mode).
- Time-sliced graph generation: large maps build across several ticks (~6ms per tick) instead of stalling a frame; any Find path call finishes an in-progress build synchronously first.
- {my} prefix on all action and condition display texts, so event sheet rows show which behavior they belong to.
0.5.0.0.changed:
- Old FindPath renamed to 'Find path to position (advanced)' — unchanged behavior, full parameter control.
- Runtime split into maintainable modules (obstacle map, graph build, pathfinding, movement, portals, hazards, navigation manager).
- Removed the dead legacy src/aces.js; ACE folder files are the single source of truth.
- Guide.md fully rewritten: scenarios-first structure, complete ACE reference tables, system + game use cases (incl. fleeing and flee-to-cover), corrected scripting docs (on()/off() listener API).
0.5.0.0.fixed:
- GraphData expressions IsNodeIsland / IsNodeLeftLedge / IsNodeRightLedge / IsTileJumpThru crashed at runtime (called methods that did not exist).
- 'Node exists at grid/world position' conditions always returned false (stale string map key).

0.5.1.0.added:
- Collision-polygon accurate solids scanning (per the documented containsPoint API): rotated/irregular solid sprites no longer over-fill their bounding box, per-tile collision polygons are honored (disabled-collision tiles scan as clear, partial polys only mark covered cells), instances with collisions disabled are skipped.
- Per-Instance graph mode warns once when used by 9+ instances on a layout (each builds its own graph; Shared is almost always the right choice at scale).
0.5.1.0.changed:
- Guide: new 'With or without the Pathfinding behavior' comparison section and 'Procedurally generated levels (best practices)' section (direct-write obstacle map pattern, timing rules, cleanup, validation, per-seed caching).
- FUTURE_FEATURES: Graph Groups design (named graph sharing to eventually replace the Shared/Per-Instance mode).
0.5.1.0.fixed:
- Horizontally flipped solid tiles were skipped by the tilemap scan (negative raw tile IDs failed the presence check).
- Instances spawned after the shared graph was built no longer trigger a full graph rebuild per spawn (late joiners inherit the built graph); wave spawners are now safe at scale.

0.6.0.0.added:
- Map Tags: instances with the same Map Tag share one navigation map, so one layout can host several shared maps (ghosts, flyers, giants). Empty tag = the default shared map.
- Portals, hazards, cell-size auto-detection, avoidance, and builds all operate per map tag.
- One map copy per map: instances share obstacle/slope/hazard data by reference.
- Map-setup actions run once per picked set; the other instances adopt the result.
- Debug warning when an instance's jump physics differ >20% from the shared graph (suggests a separate Map Tag).
- Debug aids for tag typos: console lists active tags when a new one appears; debugger shows each instance's tag.
- MapTag expression (Obstacles).
- Detect Slopes property: solid scans probe collision shapes and auto-register 45/22.5-degree slopes, no tile ID lists needed.
- AutoDetectSlopeTiles rebuilt on the documented collision API (containsPoint), with flip handling and per-shape caching.
- Hazard changes now apply automatically: costs re-bake lazily once per map per tick, O(nodes + hazard area), so hundreds of hazards stay cheap.
- Tracked hazards (AddTrackedHazard / ClearAllTrackedHazards / TrackedHazardCount): hazards that follow objects with no per-frame events and auto-remove on destroy.
- LastHazardID expression for removing or tracking a just-added hazard.
- Portal move-in-place (SetPortalPosition / SetPortalPositionFromObjects): preserves ID, type, cost, speed, and tags; connections re-wire immediately.
- Enabled property (panel bottom) plus Set enabled action and Is enabled condition; disabling freezes navigation with all state kept.
- PathEndX / PathEndY expressions: the path's actual final position (differs from the target in Nearest mode).
- BREAKING: PathTargetX/Y(type) and PathTargetGridX/Y replaced by parameterless TargetX / TargetY / TargetGridX / TargetGridY.
0.6.0.0.changed:
- Drop-in defaults: Auto-Build Graph = Auto, Detect Slopes = on, Tile Size = 32 (0 = auto-detect). Working pathfinding from a single Find path event.
- BREAKING: Graph Mode property and Per-Instance mode removed; Map Tags supersede them. Property indices after slot 5 shifted, so re-check properties in older projects.
- ACE categories reorganized to mirror the built-in Pathfinding behavior: Pathfinding, Movement, Obstacles, Hazards, Portals, Debug (IDs unchanged, saves unaffected).
- List names matched to the built-in behavior: On arrived, On failed to find path, Stop, Is moving along path, Is calculating path (IDs unchanged).
- BREAKING: Debug graph ACEs renamed with a Graph prefix (GraphNodeCount, GraphNodeAtIndex*, NearestGraphNode*, Graph node exists...) since the built-in behavior uses node to mean path waypoint. Path steps stay Waypoint*. Scripting names follow.
- Set multi-agent avoidance labels normalized to Enabled/Disabled.
- Guide: new map tags section; reference tables regrouped into the six new categories.
0.6.0.0.fixed:
- Instances that never ran a map-setup action (late spawns, second object types) had no grid dimensions, silently breaking node lookups; map state is now shared to every subscriber.
- Starting a graph build cancels another instance's in-flight build for the same map instead of both mutating the shared graph.
- Multi-agent avoidance spatial hash is cached per map instead of globally.
- Hazards added or removed mid-game had no effect until a full graph rebuild.
- Hazard IDs now come from a shared counter; per-instance counters could collide in shared maps.
- Undocumented-API audit: layout name replaces layout.uid (read undefined), isJumping replaces the nonexistent isRising, jumpSustain normalized for the seconds-vs-milliseconds ambiguity.

0.7.0.0.added:
- Shortest Distance now uses a time model: each jump carries a flat stop penalty (brake, re-center, re-launch) and momentum jumps carry no premium under it, so it skips intermediate platforms with momentum jumps where that is faster.
- Momentum (run-up) jumps: gaps too wide for a standstill jump are automatically re-validated with a run-up launch from the tile edge (~45% more horizontal range), including launches from slope tops. The AI backs up, sprints, and leaps - no events needed; connections show as [mom] in debug path logs.
- Path strategies now shape the A* search itself (not just the final candidate pick), so strategies genuinely diverge wherever the map offers real alternatives.
- Safest Route scales fall costs with drop height and jump costs with jump length (both capped), preferring chained short hops and drops via intermediate ledges over single long leaps and falls.
- Off-course landing recovery: landing far from a jump/fall waypoint re-paths immediately instead of waiting out the stuck timer.
- Debug aids for arc misses: compact per-arc logs (departure and first wall contact for each jump/fall) and fall-braking markers.
- Isolated-region warning (debug): after each graph build, the console names any node clusters that cannot reach the rest of the map, so unreachable pockets are diagnosed at build time instead of failing silently.
0.7.0.0.changed:
- Simplest Path is rebranded and reworked as Ground-Hugging: walking is free, jumps cost 4x per pixel plus a large flat fee, falls 2x plus a smaller fee - the AI walks long detours and only leaves the ground when the map gives it no choice. The internal key stays simplest, so saved projects and scripts are unaffected.
- Jump validation is now a kinematic flight simulation of the arc the character actually flies: full jump height when Jump Sustain is 0, executor-style acceleration and braking, harmless ceiling bonks, fatal wall hits. Replaces the minimal-peak Bezier sweep that approved jumps the character could not physically make (it then flew into walls and dropped short).
- Upward jumps respect the kinematic height/distance envelope: near-max height leaves near-zero horizontal range, so max-height-AND-max-distance corner jumps are no longer generated.
- Diagonal fall clearance accounts for the character's half-height, so falls no longer thread gaps that clip the head on a solid's corner mid-arc.
- Jumps to lower targets are only downgraded to walk-off falls when plain fall physics can actually cover the horizontal distance; otherwise the jump arc is kept.
0.7.0.0.fixed:
- The Path Strategy property was ignored: a leftover constructor default overwrote it, so every instance always ran Balanced (only the Set path strategy action worked).
- Horizontal braking read the Platform behavior's overall speed, which includes vertical fall speed - mid-fall stopping distances ballooned, drift input cut out at the ledge, and long diagonal falls dropped short into pits. All braking now uses the horizontal velocity (vectorX).
- Characters could park on a ledge corner forever when arrival braking stopped them inside the fall dead zone while still standing above the drop; they now creep off the edge.
- Jump drift had no mid-air braking (input flip-flopped around the target X), so jumps onto one-tile islands missed or landed depending on oscillation phase.

0.8.0.0.added:
- Crowd Arrivals (property + Set crowd arrivals action + Is crowd arrivals enabled condition): characters pathing to the same position each claim a landing node; later arrivals retarget to the nearest unclaimed neighbor, so packs tile around a target instead of stacking on one pixel. Per map tag.
- Claims are kept while standing at the reserved spot and released on Stop, pathing elsewhere, disable, destroy, and graph rebuilds. TargetX/Y report the requested position; PathEndX/Y show the reserved spot.
- Idle Separation (property + Set idle separation action + IdleSeparation expression): personal space in pixels for characters with no active path; any closer and they gently push apart. Ledge-safe, never interferes with path following, 0 = off, works with or without Crowd Arrivals.
- Separation give-up: when the crowd is too dense to satisfy the spacing, characters stop trying after the give-up time (1.2s default; Set separation give-up time action + SeparationGiveUpTime expression) and rest for Separation Cooldown seconds (property + action + expression; 0 = never rest).
- Teleports, portals, event repositioning, and arriving from a path reset the give-up state, so freshly placed or re-gathered characters always get a fresh separation attempt.
0.8.0.0.changed:
- BREAKING: the Crowd Arrivals, Idle Separation, and Separation Cooldown properties are inserted before Enabled (which stays last, per C3 convention), so property indices after slot 16 shifted - projects saved with 0.7.0.0 must re-check this behavior's properties after updating.
- Guide: crowd arrivals and idle separation section, three new full examples (zombie horde surround, squad rally point with PathEndX markers, guard-post/rat-nest settle tuning), and five new genre sketches (barricade siege, fireteam squad, pet collection, arena lineup, town crowds).
- All ACE parameter descriptions rewritten in the built-in behaviors' vocabulary ('The X co-ordinate, in pixels.', 'Whether to enable or disable...'), and em-dashes removed from every ACE and property description.
- Addon description rewritten: briefer, and now mentions momentum jumps and crowd handling.

0.9.0.0.added:
- Ledge-to-ledge patrolling: Start patrol walks the current platform end to end with a dwell at each turn, finding the ends automatically from the graph's ledges and walls (walkable slopes included). Edge distance makes the character turn that many pixels short of each edge (0 = edge to edge); a distance too big for the platform parks it at the middle, never off a ledge.
- Patrol companions: Stop patrol action, Is patrolling condition, On patrol end reached / On patrol dwell started / On patrol dwell finished triggers, PatrolDirection expression. The dwell triggers bracket the wait at each end for animation swaps. Any Find path call ends the patrol, so chase-and-return guards need no bookkeeping.
- Patrols self-heal: knocked airborne waits for landing, landing on a different platform re-anchors to its ends, single-tile islands stand still. Patrol state survives savegames.
- Find path to nearest ledge action (Left / Right / Any) with a custom distance to stop back from the edge (0 = on the edge), plus NearestLedgeLeftX/Y and NearestLedgeRightX/Y expressions. New PathFailReason value: no_ledge_found.
- Find path to side of object action: stop beside a target at a custom distance (0 = flush beside it; both widths always cleared), for melee spacing, firing range, or charge-up run-up room; Any picks the nearer side and falls back if it has no ground.
- On side of object reached trigger + ReachedObjectSide expression (-1 left, 1 right): fires only when a side-of-object arrival genuinely lands beside the target at the requested distance, so attack logic never triggers from a stopped-short Nearest-mode arrival.
- Is on same platform as object condition + OnSamePlatform(x, y) expression: true when the target is reachable by walking alone, no jumps or falls (same connected stretch of ground, slopes included). For picking walk-to targets or choosing between walking and lunging.
- Find object on same platform action (Nearest / Furthest) + PlatformObjectUID expression: searches the object's picked instances for the closest or farthest one on the character's platform; pick the result with System's Pick by unique ID (-1 = none found).
- Pathing actions now work from On start of layout (which runs before the behavior's first tick): Find path (all variants), Start patrol, and Jump toward position initialize the behavior and build the graph synchronously when called early. Portal and hazard actions work there too, registering into the shared map and connecting when the graph builds. No more waiting for On navigation graph generated to issue the first command or set up the level.
- Two new Path Strategy presets (appended, index-safe): No Falling never descends by jumping or falling, taking slopes and portals down instead (heavy units, fall damage); Walk Only never jumps or falls at all, staying on its own platform and getting as close to off-platform targets as its ground allows. Both are search-time guarantees, not cost preferences.
- Set max traversal drop action + MaxTraversalDrop expression: a per-character descent limit in pixels that excludes airborne edges with a larger net drop (-1 = no limit). Raises No Falling's allowance (e.g. to a fall-damage-safe height) and works standalone with any strategy.
0.9.0.0.changed:
- BREAKING: built-in Pathfinding behavior support removed; the addon is now fully standalone. The map copy relied on the Pathfinding behavior's undocumented .map interface, and the native Solid/Jump-thru scan is synchronous, collision-polygon accurate, and represents one-way platforms (the copy never could). Removed ACEs: UsePathfindingObstacleMap, Is setting up Pathfinding, On Pathfinding map ready / failed / timeout, WaitTickCount.
- BREAKING: Auto-Build Graph combo reduced to Off / Auto (Auto = scan Solid/Jump-thru objects; the From Pathfinding and From Solids options are gone). Re-check the property in projects saved with 0.8.x.
- Tile Size auto-detect (0) now reads the solid tilemap's tile size (the Pathfinding Cell Size source is gone with the dependency).
- BREAKING: the 'Generate navigation graph' action is removed; it had become identical to 'Regenerate navigation graph' once the async Pathfinding source was gone. Regenerate now covers both first builds after manual tile setup and rebuilds after level changes.
- The runtime now uses only documented Construct scripting and addon SDK APIs (audited this version; the removed Pathfinding map copy was the last undocumented interface), so future C3 releases cannot silently break the addon's internals.
- The two dozen longest ACE descriptions tightened to one or two sentences (behavior plus the key caveat; the Guide keeps the detail).
- Every combo parameter now explains each of its options in the parameter description (shown while the combo is focused), e.g. what Left / Right / Any mean for ledge facing, or which hazards Shapes vs Tracked only covers.
- BREAKING: ten actions merged into three combo actions plus one absorption, with no capability lost: Clear hazards (Which: Shapes / Tiles / Tracked / Everything) replaces the three ClearAll* hazard actions and gains an Everything option; Set movement limit (Jump height / Jump distance / Fall distance) replaces the three SetMax* actions; Set separation setting (Distance / Cooldown / Give-up time) replaces the three separation setters; RemovePortalsByTag with an empty tag replaces ClearAllPortals.
- Guide: platform patrol example is now one action; fourteen new examples (sentry overwatch, melee flanking, cliff-dive stunt, rampart guard, archer firing distance, lever worker, wolf pack pincer, charge-up attack, same-platform chest looting, patrol shift change, fall-damage knight, counter-bound shopkeeper, leashed guard dog, drop-limited cat), seventeen new genre sketches, and a 'Restricting how a character may travel' system use case; new 'Pathing from On start of layout' section; obstacle-map chapter rewritten without the Pathfinding source; portal and hazard docs updated (added any time including On start of layout, owned by the map for the whole layout, rebuilding a lift after removing its portals); procedural-level rules gain the On start of layout ordering catch and a new rule on keeping generated levels inside the map area.
0.9.0.0.fixed:
- Regenerate navigation graph called while a time-sliced build was in progress was silently swallowed: the in-flight build completed and cleared the dirty flag. The action now cancels the in-flight build first.
- Portals and hazards added before the behavior's first tick (e.g. in On start of layout) were stored in the calling instance's private table instead of the shared map, and were silently lost whenever another instance subscribed to the map first (multiple characters, or picking one instance by UID). Portal and hazard actions now initialize the behavior first, so they work from On start of layout in every setup.
- Portal IDs came from a per-character counter, so two characters on the same map could hand out the same ID and one portal silently replaced another (its graph links then pointed at the wrong portal). IDs are now unique across all characters, like hazard IDs.
- Running a portal or elevator-stop action on an object type with several instances now registers the portal once and gives every instance the same LastPortalID, so Set portal cost and Remove portal act on the one real portal instead of one of several copies.
- Portals, hazards, and elevator groups were stored on whichever character joined the map first, so destroying that one character erased every portal and hazard on the map (paths could still route through the vanished portals) and savegames kept them only in that character's data. They are now stored per map and last until the layout ends, so a wave game whose characters all die between waves keeps its doors and hazards, and every character saves the full set.
- Elevator stops were private to the character that added them, so a stop added through another character did not connect to the group's existing floors. Elevator groups are now shared per map, adding a stop at an existing stop's position is ignored, Remove portals by tag with an empty tag now also clears elevator groups, as documented, and removing a lift's portals by tag or ID lets its stops be added again later (for example after a power outage).
- Remove portal at object on an object type with several instances removed one portal per instance (the closest, then the next closest, and so on). It now removes only the closest portal.
- Tiles at the left and right edges of the map could be linked straight across the map: a neighbour lookup one column past the edge wrapped into the opposite edge of the row above or below. Characters then walked into the layout edge and re-pathed in a loop. Positions just outside the map also resolved to the wrong side instead of failing. Out-of-map lookups now find nothing.
